language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I’m Chip.
Hello, I’m Thomas and this is Bigeye.
Welcome to the Fantastic Fish Race!  Together we will race around the world,
competing against other teams. The first team to arrive at the final destination wins!
Our job is to swim fast, but we need you to direct us. You’re the navigator!
A navigator alerts us to what lies ahead, where to turn, and what obstacles to look out for.
Good navigators use a compass. It’s an important tool!
It tells us which way is north and where to find east, south and west.
Together, these are known as the four cardinal points of the compass.
As a navigator you also need to know the intermediate directions:
northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest.
This will help you describe the location of places in relation to other places.
As the navigator, you also need to be able to use a coordinate plane.
Coordinate planes help us easily identify an object on a map. Ready? Set? Let’s race!
To help you remember the directions on a compass, this is a good tip:
Nobody Ever Swallows Whales.
